issue_title: Filter the runs list by status, repository and label together
issue_body: Operators can only list runs by one status today. Let the runs list filter on any combination of status, repository and label, and show the per-status counts above the list.

plan.summary: Add combinable status, repository and label filters to the runs list and a per-status count, through the run store and the runs handler.

approach.description: Add a CountRunsByStatus query to backend/internal/run/queries.sql for the per-status header and regenerate the db package with sqlc generate.

Add ListRunsFiltered to backend/internal/run/postgres.go: it appends a WHERE condition for each filter the caller set and runs the assembled SQL string through the pgxpool directly, because a filter set that varies per request does not fit a static generated query; every value is bound as a positional parameter.

Accept status, repo and label query parameters on GET /v0/runs in backend/internal/server/runs.go, call the new filtered list method and CountRunsByStatus, and document the parameters and the counts field in docs/api/v0.openapi.yaml and docs/api/v0.md.
Add store tests on the shared test Postgres for each filter alone, all three together and none, and a handler test for the counts field.

verification.test_strategy: Store tests on the shared test Postgres for every filter combination, plus handler tests for the query parameters and the counts field.
verification.rollback_plan: Revert the PR; the parameters are optional and an unfiltered list is unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.statement: GET /v0/runs with status, repo and label all set returns only the runs matching all three.
The runs list response carries the number of runs in each status.

defect_phrases: runs the assembled SQL string through the pgxpool directly
does not fit a static generated query

catching_examples.note: Step 2 runs an assembled SQL string through the pgxpool directly. ADR-002 decides that queries live in backend/internal/<feature>/queries.sql with sqlc generating the typed Go, so this bypasses sqlc. Express the optional filters with sqlc.narg parameters in queries.sql instead.
ListRunsFiltered bypasses sqlc: under ADR-002 every database query is visible in a *.sql file and type-checked by the generator.
The assembled SQL in the run store sits outside queries.sql, which ADR-002's Decision rules out for backend queries.

non_catching_examples.note: Step 2: the filter design is ambiguous.
Step 2 adds a list query over runs; ADR-006 makes production rollback forward-only, so confirm the filter columns need no new migration.
Step 2 builds the WHERE clause from request input; keep every filter value a bound parameter and add a test with a quote in the label.
ac-filters-combine does not say whether a request with no filter lists every run.
ListRunsFiltered has no test for a label that matches nothing.
